drug_class: Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM) / Fertility Agent
purpose: Clomiphene is used to help women who are having trouble getting pregnant because they are not ovulating regularly or at all. It stimulates the ovaries to release an egg each month. It is one of the most commonly prescribed first-step fertility treatments.
how_it_works: Your body has a hormone system that tells your ovaries when to release an egg. Clomiphene works by blocking estrogen signals in the brain, which tricks your brain into thinking estrogen levels are low. This causes your brain to send stronger signals to your ovaries, encouraging them to grow and release an egg.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes, mood swings, bloating, breast tenderness, nausea, and headaches are the most common side effects. Some women may also notice blurred or slightly changed vision. You may also feel pelvic pressure or mild cramping around the time your ovaries are being stimulated.
warnings: There is a small increased chance of having twins or more babies when taking this medication. In rare cases, the ovaries can become overstimulated and swollen, causing serious pain — call your doctor right away if you have severe pelvic pain or bloating. Do not take this medicine if you are already pregnant. Long-term use beyond 6 cycles is generally not recommended. Let your doctor know if you have liver problems, ovarian cysts, or unusual vaginal bleeding.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg taken once a day for 5 days, typically starting on day 3, 4, or 5 of your menstrual cycle. If needed, your doctor may increase the dose to 100 mg in future cycles. Your doctor will monitor you with ultrasound or blood tests to see how your body is responding.
